article.hook: A door opens and you hesitate, hand frozen just before the latch. The North Node in Cancer pulls us toward the places where care waits - if only we stop pushing the door shut. This is about learning how to stay when it’s easier to leave.
article.lived: Over the next year and a half, the pull to tend your personal space and inner life grows persistent. You’ll notice moments when you pause before answering a text or before speaking at a family dinner, weighing whether to share more, ask for help, or soften your stance. We’re all adjusting to the discomfort of less control and more vulnerability in familiar places, like making time for a sibling or rearranging your home to invite closeness instead of keeping things distant.
article.turn: The problem comes when tending becomes clinging: insisting on care only if it’s exactly your way, or retreating behind walls that get thicker with each refusal. You can’t nurture something that’s locked away, and no one can care for you if you’re busy shutting the door. Letting people in means risking the mess and the noise - and stopping the quiet judgment that ‘they don’t get it.’
moves: Make one small change in your living space that invites someone else’s presence this week.
Ask someone to share a memory that means something to them and listen without planning a response.
When you want to pull away, say why instead of folding inward silently.
